correctness.rationale: For every integer k>=2, the explicit selected positions meet each possible factor type by monotonic zero-run lengths and alternating-power coverage. Uniquely occurring gap factors plus one terminal factor for even k or two terminal factors for odd k have disjoint occurrence intervals of precisely the target cardinality. All intervals and exceptional k=2,3 are checked. The standard-library checker exhaustively checks factor coverage through k=9 and lower-bound witnesses through k=10 from the same packaged source; the symbolic proof establishes the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: Schaeffer–Shallit's Theorem 8 already gives the dyadic upper cardinality, explicitly without a matching lower bound. The present disjoint unique-occurrence witnesses establish equality at all even and odd dyadic lengths. The 2026 greedy experiment provides a motivating performance benchmark, not an exact optimum theorem. Searches of relevant primary literature and mathematical research summaries found no implication covering the new lower bound; independent priority remains unverified.

value.rationale: Determines the exact minimum string-attractor size, with the correct additive term for all dyadic lengths, of a classical 2-automatic sparse word; this natural invariant previously had a matching-size construction but lacked an identified exact dyadic lower bound. The sharp uniqueness certificates, with parity-dependent terminal obstruction, precisely quantify a factor-two asymptotic gap from the k-position algorithmic construction in a 2026 experimental benchmark. The claim is not a numerical extrapolation and is not an arbitrary finite slice.
